title: TT-LoRA MoE: Using Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning and Sparse Mixture-Of-Experts
problem: Large model deployments face scalability challenges; MoE approaches suffer from computational overhead as expert counts grow
motivation: Enable efficient multi-task inference by combining parameter-efficient fine-tuning with sparse expert routing; reduce model footprint and computational cost
method: The approach trains task-specific expert adapters using tensor-train decomposition (a compression technique that factorizes matrices into sequences of smaller operations), keeping each expert compact for efficient deployment. Then it trains a separate router that evaluates each input using base model representations and picks exactly one expert to apply, reducing computational overhead by only running the selected expert rather than combining multiple experts.
key_novelty: It trains compact expert adapters using tensor-train compression, then trains a separate router to select which expert to use, while keeping the experts frozen so that different tasks don't interfere with each other's learned representations.
contributions: Parameter-efficient expert adaptation using tensor-train decomposition
Separate MoE router training eliminating catastrophic forgetting
Extreme parameter reduction: 2% of LoRA, 0.3% of Adapters, 0.03% of AdapterFusion
4% average improvement over AdapterFusion in multi-task setting

metrics.parameter_efficiency: 2% of LoRA, 0.3% of Adapters, 0.03% of AdapterFusion

limitations: Abstract lacks details on specific benchmarks, absolute performance metrics, and computational cost comparison
